cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: AI chatbots are actively steering consumers away from purchases
stories.plain: A new survey finds 81% of shoppers using AI chatbots have been talked out of a purchase by the AI itself. This changes the visibility game entirely — brands can no longer rely on paid or organic reach alone if the AI layer is filtering them out at the moment of decision. Directly relevant to GEO and agentic decisioning strategy.

stories.head: AI search is rewriting brand visibility — earned media is becoming infrastructure
stories.plain: The piece argues that ranking in AI-generated answers now depends on credibility signals — reviews, citations, third-party coverage — not just SEO. Brands that ignore this shift risk invisibility inside AI responses. A practical framing for marketers who need to understand why GEO is a budget-level decision, not just a technical tweak.

stories.head: Marketing automation fails without recent buyer context, new analysis warns
stories.plain: When automation platforms miss recent buyer signals — a support ticket, a browse session, a return — messaging misfires and damages trust. The piece makes a clear case for connecting CDP-level context to engagement workflows in real time. Relevant to anyone buying or building marketing automation or CEP tooling in 2026.

stories.head: Stensul integrates governed AI campaign creation with Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next
stories.plain: Stensul's beta integration lets AI agents create and personalize campaigns inside Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next, but keeps human-defined guardrails in place before activation. This is a concrete example of governed agentic creation hitting a major enterprise platform — a signal of where the CEP market is heading on AI governance.

stories.head: Vibe opens connected TV ad platform to AI agents via Claude, ChatGPT and APIs
stories.plain: Vibe now lets advertisers launch and manage streaming TV campaigns directly from AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT, or via API. This is an early but real example of agentic decisioning crossing into paid media buying — the AI doesn't just recommend, it executes. Worth watching as a template for how ad platforms open to agent orchestration.

stories.head: AI is telling consumers not to buy your product
stories.plain: Nearly 81% of shoppers using AI chatbots have been talked out of a purchase by the AI itself. This reframes the GEO problem: it's not just about showing up in AI answers, it's about whether the AI recommends or discourages your product. Marketers now have a new adversarial channel to understand and manage.

stories.head: HubSpot rebuilds its platform around AI agents
stories.plain: HubSpot redesigned Breeze Assistant so it coordinates multiple AI agents using a self-updating CRM as shared context. This is a platform-level architectural shift — not a feature add — that changes how marketing, sales, and service AI tasks are bought and run inside a single vendor ecosystem.

stories.head: Does anyone understand the CDP market anymore?
stories.plain: BlueConic's CEO explains how AI agents and M&A have fundamentally reshaped the CDP category over three years. For buyers, the vendor landscape is now harder to navigate; for builders, CDPs must now serve as the data backbone for agentic systems, not just segmentation tools.

stories.head: The problem with AI doing exactly what you ask
stories.plain: AI agents can cause serious harm without going rogue — just by optimizing a badly written goal. This piece tackles the governance gap between what marketers intend and what agents actually pursue, making objective-setting and oversight a critical new skill for anyone deploying agentic systems.

stories.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Brand Visibility. Earned Media Is Becoming Infrastructure.
stories.plain: The article argues that the competitive question has shifted from search rankings to whether AI models treat your brand as credible enough to cite. Earned media — press, reviews, authoritative mentions — is now structural marketing infrastructure, not a PR bonus, changing how brand budgets should be allocated.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Reshaping the Stack — Platforms Rebuild Around Them
body: HubSpot's full platform rebuild around AI agents is not a feature release — it is a signal that the foundational architecture of MarTech is changing. Salesforce, Stonly, Vibe, and MoEngage are all shipping agent-native capabilities in the same window, suggesting a broad platform-layer shift, not isolated experiments.

For decision-makers, this means vendor selection criteria must now include agent governance and interoperability, not just feature checklists. The question is no longer whether your stack supports AI — it is whether it was designed to be orchestrated by agents at runtime.

themes.head: AI Search Is the New Gatekeeper — and It May Recommend Against You
body: AI-powered search and answer engines are now making purchase recommendations on behalf of consumers — and those recommendations frequently exclude or actively discourage brands that have not optimized for machine-readable signals. Earned media is becoming infrastructure, not a nice-to-have PR outcome, because it feeds the training and retrieval layers that shape AI answers.

Marketers built for click-through visibility are flying blind in this environment. The decision that changes here is where to allocate content & PR budget: authority signals that AI surfaces must now sit alongside paid search in performance planning.

themes.head: Speed Without Structure: Faster AI, Worse Outcomes
body: Three separate pieces this month converge on the same warning: AI executing a flawed brief faster, with less context, and against the wrong metric amplifies existing problems rather than fixing them. Process debt compounds at AI speed. The articles on AI doing exactly what you ask, on measuring AI against the wrong goal, and on automation needing more context all describe the same failure mode from different angles.

The practical implication is that AI readiness audits must precede AI deployment. Governance frameworks, prompt design, and success metrics need to be resolved before throughput is accelerated — otherwise teams are scaling noise, not signal.
ev: MarTech · problem with AI doing what you ask

themes.head: Agent Ownership & Governance Gaps Are Becoming Liability
body: Once an AI agent is live — running ad accounts, handling customer service, or triggering workflows — the question of who is accountable for its decisions becomes urgent and largely unanswered. The conversation about agent ownership post-launch is paired this month with IAB Tech Lab's new programmatic rules and Stensul's governed content creation inside Salesforce, signalling that the industry is starting to legislate and architect around this gap.

For marketing ops teams, this is a staffing & policy question as much as a technology one. Role definitions, audit trails, and override protocols need to exist before agents touch live revenue systems — and most organizations have not written them yet.

MarTech · IAB Tech Lab programmatic rules

themes.head: The CDP & Data Layer Is Quietly Fragmenting Again
body: The CDP category — already complicated — is fracturing further as AI agents demand richer, real-time context that most customer data platforms were not built to supply. The piece asking whether anyone understands the CDP market lands alongside a separate argument that marketing automation needs more context, pointing to the same underlying data architecture problem.

Decisions about CDP vendor selection or consolidation can no longer be deferred. The context layer that feeds AI agents is only as good as the data infrastructure underneath it, and teams that have postponed that investment will find agent deployments underperforming regardless of which platform they choose.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the pattern is the same: AI amplifies whatever is already broken — in processes, in data, in governance, and in brand visibility — so the most urgent decisions are structural, not technological.
